note: Napoleon adapter of the UI scale stop-gap (J66, J67, D40): factors 1.25, 1.5 and 2.0 (3840x2160 = 2 x 1080; 2560x1440 at 1.25 or 1.5), one installed at a time. Packs are movie packs named in discovery/napoleon/games.json mod_packs.
resolution_factor_note: the factor the installer picks for a resolution (1080p: none, vanilla). 2560x1440: 1.25 until the J67 PC slot's 1440p shots; `wsc uiscale check --factor 1.5 --height 1440` loses no content against 1080p (six front-end pages bleed their 1280x961 background by 1 vanilla px), so 1.5 is allowed by the check and the shots decide (brief rule: 1.5 only if no loss and its shots read better). Both are built.
work_note: the work folders are not configured here (J79): cli.py takes <state>\uiscale\work and the masters from <state>\upscale\work, with <state> from tools/pc_state.py (harness/napoleon/adapter.json state_dir, or $NAPOLEON_STATE_DIR); --work overrides the first
art_roles_note: J36 roles resampled from the 2.5x masters; loading_screen stays 1x (engine-drawn, J67) and cursor is left vanilla (Empire). Textures a vanilla layout or template names with no master are Lanczos 2x from vanilla.
art_keep_vanilla_note: path substrings (lower case) never scaled: engine pixel-UV helpers, the 1-px progress fill (the engine multiplies progress by its width), loading screens and cursors (J67)
font_faces_note: the first that exists: the vendored face (D42, committed by J68; OFL text in uiscale/fonts/OFL.txt), else the empire-remastered clone read in place (the same file, sha256 822a6621...), kept only as a fallback
